### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 81 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9856cbc84b7d5e88752b039dff0ed9d2ee8412a5` — the merge of head `329815488ac87fac89f1dc1341c30f2b6a32c3fb` into base `b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9856cbc84b7d5e88752b039dff0ed9d2ee8412a5 && git checkout 9856cbc84b7d5e88752b039dff0ed9d2ee8412a5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017 329815488ac87fac89f1dc1341c30f2b6a32c3fb && git checkout -B drift-repro b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017 && git merge --no-ff 329815488ac87fac89f1dc1341c30f2b6a32c3fb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b358e7995e6f5a04a7e231abb8d4628d61e9a017` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` + `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` on `main` (`RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH`, `unreferencedResidualPicklistRefusal` and its wording, `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects`, the `register` order), `packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts` (`collectManifestPicklistReferences`, `manifestSources`, `collectPicklistReferences`), `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`, the residual-rule header this diff extends), `packages/metadata/src/view-container-name.ts` and `packages/objectql/src/view-container-name-refusal.ts` (how `viewContainerNameRefusal` is shared), `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.boot-parity.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts` (`artifactPackages`), `packages/cli/src/utils/view-container-names.ts` (the precedent import), `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` and `compile.ts` (the two call sites), `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` (the GATES and NOT_A_GATE rosters), `packages/cli/package.json` (dependencies), `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` (`UNIT_FILES`), `.changeset/28248-validate-residual-picklist.md`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`. `hits` is the one `stack.zod.ts` docblock; every other path of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, read here as cited code only.

Inputs: card #28248 (body; triage 6532308421; unblock 6533130283; claim 6533173970; os-dev report 6536799895), PR #28274 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head: merge-base `361ea242` is `main`'s tip, nine files, +399/-6), the head's check-runs, and the claim 6536814763. Read-only: the tree was judged, not run.

Check-runs at 2026-10-31T01:01Z: 41 check-runs on the head. 13 `success` (`Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `TypeScript Type Check` planning leg, `filter`); 8 `skipped` (path-gated UI, docs and opt-in lanes). **20 still `in_progress` and not yet reported:** `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core (1/8)` through `(8/8)`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace` — so the aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and `Test Core` contexts have not reported, and the ADR-0087 and changeset-level gates (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`) are among them. The verdict below is on the diff; the landing waits on those. PR `mergeable_state: blocked` (draft, checks pending).

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged in the tree:

1. **`os validate` and `os build` now refuse a composed stack whose residual holds a picklist that no object field the engine registers names** — right, and the card's first Wanted. `findUnreferencedResidualPicklists` returns `[]` without a `packages` key, reads the residual through `unclaimedTopLevel` from `@objectstack/metadata` (the one copy; not re-derived, as `view-container-names.ts` already reads it), takes its `picklist` entries, and builds "named" from each body (`artifactPackages(parsed)[i].body`, which is `packages[i].manifest` — the same bodies `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` hands the boot) plus the residual's own `object` entries. That is the engine's set on `main` (`[...bodies, { objects: residualObjects }]`). One finding per list, `severity: 'error'`, `rule: picklist-residual-unreferenced`, `path: picklists[i]` from the residual entry's own `field`/`index`. Both doors call `judgePicklistReferences` ahead of every artifact write (`compile.ts` step 3a-bis; the artifact write is far below), so `os build` writes nothing for a refused stack and `--json` carries the finding in `errors` unchanged in shape.
2. **The named-walk matches the engine's reader** — right. `fieldPicklistNamesOf` walks `objects` and `objectExtensions` of the source and of each plain-object entry of its nested `plugins[]`, in both field spellings, reading the `picklist` key as a non-empty string — `collectManifestPicklistReferences` over `manifestSources` does the same. The one difference is that the CLI also accepts a record-shaped `objectExtensions` where the engine reads an array only; the stack schema declares `objectExtensions` as an array, so on a parsed stack the shape is unreachable and the sets are equal.
3. **The wording is the engine's, byte for byte, for one list** — right. `residualPicklistWording(name, owner).judgement + ' ' + .prescription` equals the engine's singular message on `main` character for character (the parenthesis, the "nothing said" sentence, the three remedies and the listed-and-not-served aside included), with the same literal fallback for a stack with no id. For several residual lists the engine says one plural sentence and the door emits one singular finding per list; that is the door's per-item shape, the parity pin is scoped to single-list stacks by its own docblock, and the remedy is identical either way.
4. **The three cases the boot does not refuse are not refused here** — right. A residual object's field naming the list keeps it out of "named"'s complement (CONTROL pinned, unit and parity); a body's field naming it is `picklist-reference-unknown` as before and not this rule (CONTROL pinned); a body-declared list, repeated on the top level or not, is claimed and never residual (CONTROL pinned, unit and parity); a stack without `packages[]` returns before `unclaimedTopLevel` (CONTROL pinned, unit and parity).
5. **The text face's heading** — `picklistRefusalHeading` prints the previous sentence byte-identically when only reference refusals are present (pinned), names a residual refusal as the boot's, and joins both; `--json` does not read it. Right, and presentation only (⑥).
6. **The gate-parity ledger** — `picklistRefusalHeading` is added to `NOT_A_GATE` beside `printPicklistReferenceNotices`; `judgePicklistReferences` was already a GATE row, so the new refusal rides an existing gate both doors run. Right: without this row the ledger would fail on the new import both doors share, and the row is a true classification.
7. **The boot-parity test** — boots a real `ObjectKernel` with the real `ObjectQLPlugin` and a registering plugin that hands `{ ...manifest, ...stack }` to the `manifest` service in `init()`, the way `AppPlugin` does; asserts `INVALID_METADATA` and `message === door.message + ' ' + door.hint` on four refused stacks and no such refusal on four controls. `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/core` are `dependencies` of `packages/cli` already (`os serve` boots a kernel), so the import is not a hoisting accident; the file sits under `src/utils/*.test.ts`, which the walk behind `UNIT_FILES` collects. Right.
8. **Prose** — the residual-rule header in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` and the `stack.zod.ts` docblock gain the picklist line (④). Not a `.describe()`, so no generated artifact moves.
9. **No published schema, export, route or boot behaviour changes.** The engine is untouched; `packages/spec` changes one comment; `@objectstack/cli` gains one exported rule id and one exported heading function.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28248-validate-residual-picklist.md`: `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `@objectstack/metadata` `patch`, `@objectstack/spec` `patch`; body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial and identical to the PR body's two lines. The metadata and spec bumps carry comment-only hunks — over-declared rather than wrong; `skip-changeset` was never available because `@objectstack/cli` publishes behaviour.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right, and it is the reader's own spelling for this case.** `clause2-line.mjs` defines the four combinations: `no (narrowing)` is "NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm"; `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". This diff widens nothing (the value `no` is truthful) and `os build` now stops writing an artifact it wrote before (the arm is owed), and AGENTS.md step 3 admits `no` with the `(narrowing)` arm (only `no (widening)` is malformed). The claim expected a bare `no`; the dev's arm is the stricter and more honest reading, and the title's `!`, the scoped **BREAKING** banner and the ADR-0087 marker follow from it. For the record, this is the more exact spelling than the `yes (narrowing)` the merged PR #28231 carried for a pure narrowing; both pairs grade `patch` under ruling A with `Metadata-protocol: none`, so no level was affected there.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: no key, value, type or default an author writes changes; the refusal is a tooling judgement of a composition the schema still accepts, and the prose is comments. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` admits `none` beside any arm. Level: `none` takes `patch`. Right; `Check Changeset` green.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right — nothing an author writes is retired, `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite, and the "remedy" is an authoring placement, not a FROM-to-TO rewrite. The gate that re-checks it (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`) has not reported on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- Dev flag: **arm `no (narrowing)` rather than the claim's bare `no`.** Answered in ②: right.
- Dev flag: **a contract review is owed off the `stack.zod.ts` hunk although it is prose.** Right — `reviewFace` reads the schema face off the path; this record is it, and ④ judges the docblock as the one `hits` file.
- Dev flag, and the dispatch's first question: **restating the judgement in the CLI, held by a boot-parity pin, versus exporting it the way `viewContainerNameRefusal` is shared.** Read: `viewContainerNameRefusal` is defined once in `@objectstack/metadata` (`view-container-name.ts`), re-exported by `@objectstack/objectql` (`view-container-name-refusal.ts`), and imported by the CLI from `@objectstack/objectql`; the engine's picklist judge and its reader are module-private in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` and `picklist-resolution.ts`, and the claim excluded `packages/objectql` and allowed `packages/metadata` prose only, so neither export was in reach. What the head shares is the residual rule itself (`unclaimedTopLevel`), which decides WHICH items are residual; what it restates is the named-walk and the words, and the parity pin holds the words byte-equal on a real boot and the walk equal on eight stacks, red the moment either side moves (ablation B6 is the dev's; the pin's assertion is read here). **Acceptable for this card, as a should-fix carried on a card, not a must-fix:** the repo's standing is one spelling per judgement (the residual-rule header's own "never a second copy at a door"; record 6525505738 treated a copied refusal envelope the same way and filed #28160). The restatement is the smaller evil than a `packages/objectql` edit outside the claim, and the pin makes the copy loud; but the cost is real and asymmetric — a future wording change in `packages/objectql` reds `packages/cli`'s suite, and the engine's function docblock (excluded file) does not point at the parity file. **Should-fix #2:** file the follow-up card the dev names: one exported judge (named-walk plus wording), defined once — `@objectstack/metadata` beside `unclaimedTopLevel` is the precedent's home, with `@objectstack/objectql` re-exporting as it does for the container judge — imported by both doors; the parity pin then shrinks to a smoke check or goes.
- The dispatch's second question: **is `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` a fair reading of "their tests" in the claim?** Yes. The claim's surface names "the `os validate` / `os compile` caller that reports it if needed" and "their tests"; the ledger is the test of exactly those two callers (it holds that both doors run the same gates and classifies every shared import), and the diff's one row there is forced by the new import both callers take. A ledger row is the minimal edit that keeps the callers' test true; leaving it out would red the ledger, not pass it.
- Dev flag: **the existing `picklist-reference-unknown` walk does not judge a residual object's field naming a list nobody declares, nor a body's nested `plugins[]`.** Read: right, and outside this card (that walk predates it; the residual object's field naming an undeclared list is the boot's listed-and-not-served case, reported by the boot, not refused). No action here; a card if the seat wants `os validate` to foretell that warning too.
- Dev flag: **the two should-fixes of record 6532447134 (the objectql `plugins[]` pin, the PR #28231 body) fall outside this claim.** Right; PR #28231 is merged. The CLI side of the `plugins[]` case is pinned in the unit file here, but **not in the parity file** — it is the one refused case without a boot twin. **Should-fix #3:** add it to `STACKS` in the parity test (one line), so the door's and the boot's exclusion of top-level `plugins[]` is held equal like the other three.
- Dev deviations (suites outside `os-verify-lock`, restarted gate runs): the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts this record relies on; twenty of them have not reported.
- Serial constraint: PR #28244 edits another region of `stack.zod.ts`; the head merges `main` at `361ea242` and the merge-base IS `main`'s tip, so there is nothing left to merge. Governed surfaces: none (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** (the one `hits` file: five docblock lines on `applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate`) — holds, with one should-fix. The scenario it is accepted against is the card's second Wanted: the published spec's residual-rule prose carries the picklist line the runtime enforces. Against the code it cites, each sentence: "a residual PICKLIST is kept as metadata only, never registered with the engine" — true on `main` (`RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH` excludes `picklist` from `unclaimedTopLevelItems`; the metadata door registers it; the engine never does). "When a residual object's field names it, the boot lists that object and does not serve it" — true (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` judges the field against the bodies' lists and warns). "When no object field the engine registers names it, the boot refuses the stack, and `os validate` / `os build` refuse it first" — true on this head (`unreferencedResidualPicklistRefusal` before anything registers; `judgePicklistReferences` at both doors). Placement: the one docblock where the published spec states the residual rule in general, the one the card named. Not a `.describe()`, so `check:generated` has nothing to move. Break attempt: **the docblock states two of the three lines.** The case of a package BODY's field naming a residual picklist — refused by the boot's `kernel:ready` picklist audit as "no loaded package declares", and `picklist-reference-unknown` at the doors — is stated in the metadata header this same diff writes ("when a body's field names it, the boot's picklist audit refuses that field") and omitted here. A reader of the spec's sentence "when a residual object's field names it, the boot lists that object and does not serve it" may infer that a body's field naming it serves. **Should-fix #1:** add the body-field clause to the `stack.zod.ts` docblock so the two prose surfaces say the same three lines.

The cited CLI code was read to judge the docblock's third sentence, not reviewed; what the read found is recorded in ① and ③ for the lane seat.

**Should-fixes:**
1. `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: add the third line (a body's field naming a residual picklist fails the boot's picklist audit, `picklist-reference-unknown` at the doors), as the metadata header states it.
2. File the follow-up card for one exported judgement (named-walk plus wording) defined once, `@objectstack/metadata` beside `unclaimedTopLevel` on the `viewContainerNameRefusal` precedent, imported by the engine and both doors; the restatement and most of the parity pin then go.
3. `picklist-references.boot-parity.test.ts`: add the top-level `plugins[]` stack to `STACKS`, the one refused case without a boot twin.

No must-fix. No fail-open finding: every stack this diff refuses is one the boot refuses on `main`, and every stack the boot accepts passes both doors as before.
